problems.title: Two parabola vertices share a vertical line
problems.question: The vertices of f(x)=x²+(2a+1)x and g(x)=-x²+3x-5a lie on the same vertical line. Find a.
problems.idea: Their vertex x-coordinates must agree.
steps: The first vertex has x=-(2a+1)/2. The second has x=3/2.
Equate them: -(2a+1)=3.
Thus 2a=-4 and a=-2.

problems.title: Find where an even radical is undefined
problems.question: For which x is $\sqrt[8]{(9-x^2)/(x-2)}+\sqrt{x^2+3x+10}$ undefined?
problems.idea: The second radicand is always positive; use a sign chart for the first.
formulas: An even real root requires a nonnegative radicand; a denominator cannot be zero.
steps: The first radicand has zeros at -3,3 and a forbidden denominator at 2.
Its sign is nonnegative on (-∞,-3] and (2,3].
The complement, where the full expression is undefined, is (-3,2]∪(3,∞).

problems.title: Simplify nested roots on their real domain
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt[3]{\frac ax\sqrt{\frac1{ax}\sqrt{\frac a{x^3}}}}$.
problems.idea: Establish the signs first, then use positive magnitudes for fractional powers.
formulas: The original expression requires ax>0; for positive u, (uᵐ)ⁿ=uᵐⁿ.
steps: The factors 1/x and 1/(ax) require a,x≠0, and the innermost radicand requires a and x to have the same sign. Hence ax>0.
Put A=|a|,X=|x|. The inner square root is A^(1/2)X^(-3/2).
The next root is A^(-1/4)X^(-5/4). Multiplying by a/x=A/X and taking the cube root gives A^(1/4)X^(-3/4).
Since a/x³=A/X³>0 on this domain, the result is the fourth root of a/x³.

problems.title: Combine roots with different indices
problems.question: Evaluate $\sqrt[6]{3^7\cdot4^5}\sqrt[3]{3^5\cdot4}$.
problems.idea: Convert both radicals to sixth roots.
steps: The product is ⁶√(3¹⁷·4⁷).
Extract 3¹²·4⁶, whose sixth root is 3²·4=36.
The result is 36·⁶√(3⁵·4)=36·⁶√972.
problems.answer: $36\sqrt[6]{972}$; “none of the answers” among the choices.

problems.title: Count polygon diagonals
problems.question: Find the number of diagonals of a convex n-gon.
problems.idea: Each vertex joins diagonally to every vertex except itself and its two neighbours.
steps: There are n-3 diagonal endpoints from each of n vertices.
This counts every diagonal twice, once from each end.
The total is n(n-3)/2.

problems.title: Interior angle of a regular polygon
problems.question: Find one interior angle of a regular 15-gon.
problems.idea: Subtract its equal exterior angle from a straight angle.
steps: For n=15, the exterior angle is 360°/15=24°.
The adjacent interior angle is 180°-24°=156°.

problems.title: An equilateral triangle minus its incircle
problems.question: An equilateral triangle has an incircle. The total shaded area inside the triangle but outside the circle is 3√3-π. Find the triangle area.
problems.idea: Express both areas in terms of the inradius r.
steps: The shaded area is (3√3-π)r².
It equals 3√3-π, a positive number, so r²=1.
Therefore the triangle area is 3√3.

problems.title: A square formed by alternate octagon side midpoints
problems.question: Join the midpoints of alternate sides of a regular octagon of side 2 cm. Find the resulting quadrilateral’s area.
problems.idea: Those four midpoints lie on the incircle at equal 90° spacings.
formulas: Octagon apothem r=s/[2tan22.5°]; tan22.5°=√2-1; square area from diagonal 2r is 2r².
steps: The midpoint radius is r=1/(√2-1)=√2+1.
The four alternate midpoints form a square with diagonal 2r.
Its area is 2(√2+1)²=6+4√2.

problems.title: Subtract an inscribed equilateral triangle from a square
problems.question: A circle is inscribed in a square of side 12 cm; an equilateral triangle is inscribed in that circle. Find the area inside the square but outside the triangle.
problems.idea: The circle radius is the triangle circumradius.
steps: The circle radius is R=6.
The triangle area is 3√3·36/4=27√3.
Subtract from square area 144 to obtain 144-27√3.

problems.title: Area outside a circle in a 30-60-90 triangle
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse 8 cm and an acute angle 60°. A circle is centred at the right-angle vertex with radius equal to the short leg. Find the triangle area outside the circle.
problems.idea: Locate the second intersection with the hypotenuse; the remaining region is a triangle minus a 30° sector.
formulas: Short leg=4, long leg=4√3; sector area=θr²/2 with θ in radians.
steps: Put the right-angle vertex at C=(0,0), the short-leg endpoint at A=(4,0), and B=(0,4√3).
The circle x²+y²=16 meets hypotenuse √3x+y=4√3 at A and D=(2,2√3). Ray CD makes 60° with CA, so its angle to CB is 30°.
Triangle CBD has area (4√3)·2/2=4√3. The circle occupies a sector of angle 30° inside it, of area 16π/12=4π/3.
Subtract to get 4√3-4π/3.

problems.title: Circle inscribed in a 120-degree sector
problems.question: A circle is inscribed in a 120° sector. Find its circumference divided by the outer sector arc length.
problems.idea: Relate the small radius to the sector radius using the angle bisector.
formulas: If sector radius is R and small radius r, centre distance=R-r and r=(R-r)sin60°.
steps: The small circumference is 2πr, and the 120° arc is 2πR/3.
Their ratio is 3r/R=3(2√3-3).

problems.title: Arc length from sector area
problems.question: A sector of radius 12 cm has area 18π cm². Find its arc length.
problems.idea: Use the direct relation between sector area and arc length.
steps: If the arc length is L, then 18π=12L/2=6L.
Thus L=3π.

problems.title: A regular hexagon cut from an equilateral triangle
problems.question: Three corners are cut from an equilateral triangle to leave a regular hexagon of area 4 m². Find the original triangle area.
problems.idea: All hexagon sides equal the corner triangle sides.
formulas: An equilateral triangle of triple side length has nine times the area; a regular hexagon is six equilateral triangles of its side length.
steps: Let each hexagon side be s. Each removed corner is an equilateral triangle of side s.
An original triangle side consists of three length-s parts, so it is 3s.
The original triangle has 9 small-triangle area units; the hexagon has 6.
Thus the original area is (9/6)·4=6.

problems.title: Exterior-angle sum does not depend on side count
problems.question: Find the sum of one exterior angle at each vertex of a convex 13-gon.
problems.idea: Walking once around a convex polygon turns through one full revolution.
steps: The polygon has 13 vertices, but the total turn remains one full turn.
Therefore the sum is 360°, independent of the number of sides.

problems.title: Odd numerator root, even denominator root
problems.question: Find the domain of $\sqrt[7]{3-x}/\sqrt[8]{x-2}$.
problems.idea: An odd root has no sign restriction, while the even denominator must be positive.
formulas: An odd real root exists for every real radicand; an even root requires radicand≥0 and a denominator cannot vanish.
steps: The seventh root of 3-x is defined for every real x.
The eighth root in the denominator requires x-2≥0 and cannot equal zero.
Thus x>2, with no upper bound.

problems.title: Two negative roots from a factorization
problems.question: For which a are both roots of x²+(2a+1)x+2a=0 negative?
problems.idea: Factor the quadratic.
steps: The roots are -1 and -2a.
The first is always negative. The second is strictly negative exactly when a>0.
A repeated negative root is allowed at a=1/2 unless distinctness is additionally required.

problems.title: Locate a cube root without decimal approximation
problems.question: Which unit interval contains $5\sqrt[3]2+5$?
problems.idea: Compare ∛2 with 6/5 and 7/5.
formulas: The cube function is strictly increasing.
steps: Multiply by 5 and add 5 to obtain 11<5∛2+5<12.

problems.title: Order roots by a common positive power
problems.question: Order $\sqrt3,\sqrt[3]5,\sqrt[6]{26}$ increasingly.
problems.idea: Raise them all to the sixth power.
formulas: For positive numbers, raising to a positive power preserves order.
steps: Their sixth powers are 27,25,26 respectively.
Since 25<26<27, the same order holds for the original positive roots.

problems.title: Fractional and negative exponents
problems.question: Evaluate $0.027^{-1/3}-(-1/6)^{-2}+256^{0.75}-3^{-1}+5.5^0$.
problems.idea: Convert each power to a simple value.
formulas: a⁻ⁿ=1/aⁿ for a≠0; a⁰=1; a³/⁴=(⁴√a)³ for positive a.
steps: Since 0.027=0.3³, its power is 1/0.3=10/3.
The next two powers are 36 and 64. Also 3⁻¹=1/3 and 5.5⁰=1.

problems.title: A quadratic inequality with one integer solution
problems.question: For which a does x²-2x+a<0 have exactly one integer solution?
problems.idea: The solution interval is symmetric about the integer 1.
steps: The condition is (x-1)²<1-a.
To include x=1, require a<1.
To exclude both nearest other integers 0 and 2, require 1-a≤1, hence a≥0.
Then every more distant integer is also excluded.

problems.title: Opposite-sign roots for every nonzero parameter
problems.question: What can be said about the roots of -ax²+3x+5a=0 when a≠0?
problems.idea: Use the discriminant and root product.
steps: D=9+20a²>0, so there are two distinct real roots.
Their product is 5a/(-a)=-5<0.
A negative product means one root is positive and the other negative.
problems.answer: Two real roots of opposite signs.

problems.title: A zero product of odd and even roots
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt[5]{x^2-x-6}\sqrt[4]{-x^2+6x-5}=0$.
problems.idea: The fourth root restricts the domain before either factor is set to zero.
steps: The fifth-root factor is zero at x=3 or x=-2; only 3 is in the domain.
The fourth-root factor is zero at x=1 or x=5.
All three remaining candidates make a defined product equal to zero.

problems.title: A rational sign chart with three critical points
problems.question: Solve $x(x-1)/(x-4)>-1$.
problems.idea: Move 1 to the left and combine over the original denominator.
steps: The critical values are -2,2,4; x=4 is forbidden.
The quotient is negative on (-∞,-2), positive on (-2,2), negative on (2,4), and positive on (4,∞).
Strict positivity excludes the zeros -2,2 as well.

problems.title: Choose the signs of two absolute values
problems.question: Evaluate $\sqrt{(2-\sqrt6)^2}+2|7-\sqrt{24}|+4\sqrt6+18-\sqrt{54}$.
problems.idea: Determine each expression’s sign before removing the absolute value.
steps: Since √6>2, the first term is √6-2.
Since 2√6<7, the second is 14-4√6.

problems.title: A number strictly between quadratic roots
problems.question: Give the necessary and sufficient condition for one root of x²-bx+c=0 to exceed 2 and the other to be below 2.
problems.idea: An upward-opening quadratic is negative exactly between its two real roots.
formulas: For a monic quadratic, q(t)<0 iff t lies strictly between two distinct real roots.
steps: Evaluate at the proposed intermediate point: q(2)=4-2b+c.
The required condition is q(2)<0.
This automatically ensures two distinct real roots around 2.
